phase_degeneracy.note: The de-embedded slope should read ~0 only if this run's own measured beta were exact: what the de-embedding leaves is arg t + (beta_meas - beta_true)*dL, so a non-zero value here is the de-embedding's own residual and not a property of the line -- it must never be quoted as a beta. The raw slope is the AC-7 quantity, but from ONE run it equals beta - arg(t)/dL: that assumes arg t = 0, and it is only defined modulo the branch spacing above. Neither number is an AC-7 verdict, and neither is the field of the same name in graded.json's AC-7 block: that one is taken across TWO runs, between their `s21.planes_m[1]`, over the 10.0 mm between them.

AC-7.reason: docs/design/absorbing_termination_scope.md:266 says `beta_FDTD = -d(arg S21)/dL` **from two line lengths** -- a slope in L, i.e. two runs at two lengths. This run is one length, so dL is undefined here and no proxy is substituted. grade_2b.py takes the slope across the two artefacts' own `s21.planes_m`, not a typed-in 10 mm.
AC-7.which_phase: s21.raw_phase_deg -> s21.raw_phase_rad. NOT s21.phase_deg: that one is de-embedded with this run's own measured beta, so it is flat in L only to the extent that beta is exact -- what survives is (beta_meas - beta_true)*dL, not 0 by construction (see phase_degeneracy below).

run.loaded_without_reference_note: True means no LineReference was supplied, so the cut branch degraded to zc_split = zc and line_s21(...): the line constant used to transport the port plane to the cut is the run's own zc/beta, not a load-free measurement. Stated, not hidden.

twin.alpha_np_per_m_basis: nepers per metre of AMPLITUDE decay, exp(-alpha x): emfit/ports.py:1010 LineFit.alpha, whose unit is 1/m, or dB/m as 8.685889638 * alpha.  None when the twin's stations could not support a loss fit (loss_fit or loss_fit.alpha is None), and LineReference.from_wave then uses exactly 0.0 -- a line with no modelled loss, not a measured zero.
twin.gamma_im_basis: the twin's own fitted BETA [rad/m]: gamma = alpha + 1j*beta (emfit/studies.py:1743-1749, LineReference.from_wave)
twin.station_fit_basis: station_x[-1] - station_x[0] over the stations the s11 fit actually used; shorter than station_span_m when the last station sat on the load column
twin.station_span_basis: the twin's first to last station, station_x[-1] - station_x[0]; forward_ratio refuses any other pair, so this is the span the loaded s21 was normalised over
twin.zc_basis: the twin's station_fit.z0: the impedance its own station voltages and currents imply, not the closed-form z0

s11.basis: gamma_port, the reflection moved to the port plane (emfit/studies.py:3266, declared at :1607; docstring :1527-1531).  Plane-independent: it does not move when the extraction plane moves.  modulus of B/A from fit_beta(n_wave=2), referred to z=0, plane-invariant at alpha=0, not de-embedded. phase_deg is unchanged and belongs to the one-wave station fit at the port plane, NOT to the magnitude beside it; no two-wave phase is reported because no two-wave beta is stored.
s11.validation_reason: the magnitude above is the modulus of the two-wave B/A, not the one-wave station-fit reflection (that is kept beside it as magnitude_one_wave_station_fit).  On the R=100 record it reads 0.4739 against the series-R anchor 0.51263, i.e. 7.56 percent low.  The residual disagreement is unexplained: no read of station_fit.gamma_v or of the reference construction has been done, so the status stays. Residual is configuration-dependent: 5.5% (n=64, load 20mm), 7.6% (n=54, 100 ohm), 13.8% (n=79, load 30mm). The two-wave modulus is better than one-wave but not converged -- the load's near-field extends to the last station and contaminates the fit. Moving the extraction plane further from the load, or modal projection, would reduce it. Structural note (2026-11-02): the strip mask is PEC-continuous from the port plane to the far xmax PEC wall (emfit/studies.py:2704-2712), so the load sits in series with a shorted stub instead of terminating a matched line; the series-R anchor cited above therefore does not describe this structure. See dispatch_log.md 2026-11-02.

s11_at_plane.basis: gamma_plane, the reflection at the extraction plane itself (b_cut/a_cut).  A different quantity from s11, not interchangeable; null when the record was extracted over the station span.

s21.phase_deg_basis: s21 de-embedded on the cut branch, and WHICH de-embedding it is depends on the branch.  With a twin reference -- the path these loaded runs take -- reference is not None, so s21 = raw_s21 / reference.forward_ratio(x_port, x_cut) (emfit/studies.py:3352) and line_s21 is NOT called; the delay is taken out by the reference's own measured forward amplitude ratio, rescaled to the run's span, not by this run's beta.  Only on the no-reference branch does line_s21 (emfit/studies.py:1242, called at :3354) multiply by exp(+1j*beta*distance) (emfit/ports.py:1707-1731) with this run's own measured beta. Flat in L only to the extent that beta is exact -- what the de-embedding leaves is arg t + (beta_meas - beta_true)*d, so the slope recorded in phase_degeneracy.deembedded_slope_rad_per_m is this run's de-embedding residual, NOT ~0 by construction. Not the AC-7 quantity, and not the same number as the field of that name in graded.json's AC-7 block, which differences two runs over 10.0 mm.
s21.raw_basis: operands use reference.gamma and reference.zc; raw_magnitude differs from noref raw 0.762847 by 5.8% and is not a reference-independent measurement
s21.raw_phase_deg_basis: s21_raw, no de-embedding applied: this is the AC-7 quantity, and it carries -beta*L.
